And if that weren't enough, their stores offered nothing more interesting than fucking JCPenny, of all places.

It seems silly to have to say it, but these articles keep coming out as if the authors are divorced from history. Sears was the Internet Explorer 6 of the retail industry, as far as customers were concerned. They coasted on their hardware, and then appliance and clothing, sales for so long, that once their wares had lost appeal, they were entirely unable to compete. They had apparently lost all their talent, and within a decade they had lost their loyal shoppers, and decades later nobody cares to even see what they offer. It's not that Sears is a dinosaur, for lizards can easily adapt. It's that their body had atrophied past the point of no return.

I don't have any stake n any of this other than seeing the endless articles and the endless store closings. And these are all used for political purposes, because anything ambiguous is political now. So it is important to note that Sears could have become the internet catalog of the future, or at least a good runner up, if they had wanted to. They didn't want to.
